source: CoSAI AI Shared Responsibility Framework §3.1, Draft V0.7
provenance_note: The 'provenance' field on each persona distinguishes personas published by CoSAI (provenance: cosai-core) from personas proposed independently on this site to support specific deployment topologies (provenance: proposed-extension). Extension personas are not part of the official CoSAI SRF release. See NOTICE and the vertical-controls disclaimer for the same convention applied elsewhere on this site.

personas.name: Agentic Platform & Framework Providers
personas.standard_ref: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19.5 - AI Partner (tool and framework provider)
personas.description: Provides development environments, software frameworks, and orchestration runtimes for agentic AI. Responsible for framework security, sandboxing, secure state management across multi-turn workflows, and defining cognitive architecture.
responsibilities: Ensuring framework security and sandboxing
Implementing safety controls around tool execution
Managing state in multi-turn workflows securely
Integrating APIs securely
Defining cognitive architecture for AI systems

personas.name: Application Developer
personas.standard_ref: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19.2 - AI Provider; also acts as AI Customer (§5.19.4) with respect to upstream model and platform providers
personas.description: Integrates AI models into applications, products, or services via APIs or embedded models. May perform light customization such as prompt engineering or RAG. Accountable for application-level security controls, input validation, output filtering, and user access management.
responsibilities: Implementing application-level security controls
Implementing safety controls around tool execution
Ensuring input validation and output filtering
Managing user access control mechanisms

personas.name: Data Provider
personas.description: Supplies training data, evaluation datasets, or inference data to model providers or application developers. Includes data aggregators, data marketplaces, and dataset licensors.
responsibilities: Conducting data quality assurance
Tracking data provenance and compliance
Implementing privacy protections in data handling
Managing data classification

personas.name: AI System Users
personas.assignment_note: Defined for completeness; no controls in the current finance schema assign accountability to this persona. End-user obligations in finance deployments are governed by the institution's acceptable-use policy, which falls under ai-system-governance.
personas.description: Uses AI-powered applications or services without developing or deploying the AI components. Relies on application developers and providers for security controls.
responsibilities: Adhering to appropriate use policies
Reporting issues or anomalies detected during use
Following usage guidelines to minimize data exposure

personas.name: AI System Governance
personas.standard_ref: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19.4 - AI Customer; §5.19.7 - Relevant Authority where regulatory obligations apply
personas.description: Defines security control objectives, measures implementations, and enforces compliance across the AI system lifecycle. Includes AI risk officers, compliance teams, and governance boards.
responsibilities: Establishing security and governance rules including acceptable risk levels
Evaluating security measure effectiveness across the AI lifecycle
Ensuring compliance with standards, laws, and company policies
Managing a risk register with assigned owners and remediation timelines
Overseeing incident response plans and post-incident analysis

personas.name: Model Provider
personas.description: Develops, trains, evaluates, and tunes AI/ML models including foundation models, specialized models, and domain-adapted models. Accountable for model architecture security, safety validation, and model card publication.
responsibilities: Secure and responsible model architecture design and training
Model security, safety, and performance validation
Publishing model cards with provenance, benchmarks, and intended use
Maintaining model version and vulnerability disclosures

personas.name: AI Model Serving
personas.standard_ref: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19.5 - AI Partner (platform and runtime services provider)
personas.assignment_note: Defined for completeness; no controls in the current finance schema assign accountability to this persona. L4 controls currently assign to ai-platform-provider or agentic-platform-provider. Review at v1.0 to confirm whether model-serving responsibilities warrant a separate accountability line in L4 controls.
personas.description: Provisions, manages, and secures the runtime environment that serves AI and ML model predictions at scale. Distinct from Model Provider (training/registry) and AI Platform Provider (physical infrastructure). Focused on secure orchestration and delivery of the model serving layer.
responsibilities: Managing secure API endpoints, enforcing access policies, and input validation
Executing models in isolated or confidential computing environments
Ensuring model and dataset integrity at load-time and during runtime
Monitoring and validating outputs to prevent unintended disclosures
Conducting adversarial simulations to test model serving robustness

personas.name: AI Platform Provider
personas.standard_ref: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19.5 - AI Partner (infrastructure provider); also acts as AI Provider (§5.19.2) where the platform serves application developers
personas.description: Provides infrastructure, compute resources, APIs, and platform services for AI model hosting, training, or inference. Includes cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP), MLOps platforms, and model API services.
responsibilities: Securing infrastructure and maintaining high availability
Maintaining platform-level compliance certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP)
Providing robust IAM primitives for upstream tenants
Providing configurable data residency, encryption, and region-locking capabilities
Guaranteeing uptime, incident notification, and SLAs bounding the platform's contribution to incident response

personas.name: Sovereign Participant Node
personas.standard_ref: No single ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19 role fits without modification. This persona combines the AI Customer, AI Producer, and AI Partner (data provider) roles the standard treats as separate organizations into one sovereign entity performing all three simultaneously.
personas.cross_layer_note: Deliberate deviation from the CoSAI persona pattern. Every cosai-core persona above occupies one or two adjacent layers because SRF models a vendor/customer supply chain: distinct organizations at distinct layers. A Tapestry participant is a peer, not a vendor or a customer of the consortium, so it locally instantiates the full stack: it governs its own use (L1), owns its own training data (L2), builds its own sovereign derivatives (L3), runs its own local training compute (L4), and performs local continued pre-training / fine-tuning and submits weight contributions (L5). Do not read the five-layer span as this persona having authority over the Shared Base at every layer; see accountable_to splits in the Federated-Consortium operating model in layers.json, which separate what this persona owns (Participant Sovereign Assets) from what the core owns (Shared Commons).
personas.description: A national government, cultural community, enterprise, hospital, or other institution participating in Project Tapestry as a self-governing node. Retains full control of its own data, source identities, training processes, model updates, configurations, evaluations, and derivatives unless it explicitly and voluntarily contributes an artifact to the Shared Commons. May perform Contributed CPT locally and submit only the resulting model-weight update without disclosing underlying data.
responsibilities: Retaining control of raw, curated, private, sovereign, controlled, or proprietary data (TAP-010, Participant Sovereign Assets)

Holding sufficient rights and authorization to perform local training and to permit the intended use and distribution of any resulting weight contribution (TAP-010, Weight contribution does not transfer data rights)
Not introducing legal terms into a submitted contribution that would encumber the Shared Base or reduce the rights of other participants (TAP-010, Weight contribution does not transfer data rights)
Deciding, without requiring Tapestry permission, whether to keep, deploy, license, sell, or otherwise commercialize its Sovereign Models and related services (TAP-010, Participant Sovereign Assets)
Participating in consortium governance in proportion to its role, without its contribution size becoming unilateral control (docs/work-groups/governance-participation, Initial questions)

personas.name: Consortium Core Coordinator
personas.standard_ref: No ISO/IEC 22989:2022 §5.19 role fits. The standard has no concept of a shared artifact accountable to the consortium itself rather than to any single organization.
personas.status_note: Corresponds to the body TAP-010 names as decider: 'Tapestry Governance Committee (to ratify).' As of TAP-010's Proposed status, this body is not yet formally seated. Treat this persona as provisional until governance ratification. docs/work-groups/governance-participation/README.md lists the operating model and decision-escalation path this persona depends on as an early deliverable, not yet published.
personas.description: The accountable party for the Shared Commons: the shared base model, shared training infrastructure, shared protocols and interoperability specifications, public governance rules, and certification marks. Distinct from any single participant node. Accountable for keeping Shared Commons artifacts open and independently usable, and for preventing capture of the commons by any participant, vendor, or operator.
responsibilities: Keeping Tapestry-developed source code, shared protocols, schemas, and interoperability specifications open and independently usable (TAP-010, Shared Commons commitments)

Evaluating submitted weight contributions for legality, consent, provenance, quality, safety, security, memorization, poisoning, and compatibility before acceptance into the Shared Base (TAP-010, Shared contribution and certification boundaries)
Designating the body that approves independent auditors and determines when contractual assurance is insufficient (TAP-010, Follow-on decisions; not yet resolved)

Governing use of Tapestry certification marks, compatibility claims, and governance recognition separately from ownership of private participant assets (TAP-010, Shared contribution and certification boundaries)

Preventing any participant, vendor, or operator from imposing an exclusive service, proprietary runtime, or other avoidable dependency on the Shared Commons (TAP-010, Shared Commons commitments; anti-capture-principle.md)

sector_specializations_note: A vertical may assign accountability to a sector-specific name for one of the eight canonical personas rather than to the persona itself. Those names are declared here so that every accountable_persona value in data/*-controls.json resolves to a record, and so the graph carries an explicit specializes edge back to the canonical persona. They are specializations, not additional personas: the canonical count stays at eight.

sector_specializations.name: Clinical AI Governance
sector_specializations.description: AI System Governance as constituted in a care-delivery organization: the clinical AI ethics committee, medical staff leadership, and regulatory affairs function that authorize clinical AI use and own FDA filing currency.

sector_specializations.name: Clinical Data Steward
sector_specializations.description: Data Provider as constituted for PHI: the health information management function accountable for training data consent, demographic representation, and PHI isolation in non-production environments.

sector_specializations.name: Clinical Application Developer
sector_specializations.description: Application Developer building clinical decision support: accountable for human-in-the-loop gates on high-stakes outputs, explanation coverage, and clinical workflow usability validation.

sector_specializations.name: Health Platform Provider
sector_specializations.description: AI Platform Provider operating in a healthcare setting: accountable for SMART on FHIR authorization, FHIR AuditEvent logging completeness, and PHI encryption.
